:::{#def-fitting-procedure}
#### Fitting procedure

A **fitting procedure** $\fitproc$ is a [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/functions.html#def-function) that,
given any [data set](#def-data-set) $\dataset$,
produces the [fitted model](#def-fitted-model) $\emodmem = \fitprocf{\dataset}$:

$$
\dataset
\mapsto
\emodmem
= \fitprocf{\dataset}.
$$ {#eq-fitting-procedure}

A fitting procedure is specified by these inputs:

- [model family](#def-model-family) $\modelfam$;
- [objective function](#def-objective-function) $\objfn$;
- [optimization algorithm](#def-optimization-algorithm) $\optalg$;
- [random seed](#def-random-seed) $\seed$;
- [tuning parameters](#def-tuning-parameter) $\tuning$;
- [preprocessing](#def-preprocessing) $\featmap$.

:::

:::{#rem-source-fitting-procedure}
#### Source: Fitting procedure

The [definition of a prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) takes a covariate value $x$ and a data set as the two arguments of a rule $g$.
The fitting procedure $\fitproc$ takes the same two arguments one at a time, the data set $\dataset$ first and then the covariate value $x$:
$g\paren{x; \dataset} = \fitprocf{\dataset}\paren{x}$.
@hastie2009elements [sec. 7.2] write the model estimated from a training set as $\hat f$.

:::
